prompts.label: WHAT ARE VPC CIDR BLOCKS AND SUBNETS?
prompts.placeholder: A VPC is an isolated virtual network with one or more IP address ranges. A…

reveal.text: A VPC is an isolated virtual network with one or more IP address ranges. A subnet is a non-overlapping range inside the VPC and belongs to one Availability Zone.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Plan CIDRs with enough usable addresses and no overlap with networks that must connect.

reveal.text: Plan CIDRs with enough usable addresses and no overlap with networks that must connect.

A VPC uses `10.0.0.0/16`. Public subnet A uses `10.0.1.0/24` and private subnet A uses `10.0.11.0/24`. A proposed peered VPC also uses `10.0.0.0/16`, creating overlapping CIDRs that prevent straightforward routing between them.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Peering/TGW/VPN routing problems often begin with overlapping CIDRs or insufficient subnet addresses.

reveal.text: Peering/TGW/VPN routing problems often begin with overlapping CIDRs or insufficient subnet addresses.

prompts.label: WHAT ARE ROUTE TABLES?
prompts.placeholder: A route table maps destination CIDR/prefixes to network targets. Routing uses the most specific matching…

reveal.text: A route table maps destination CIDR/prefixes to network targets. Routing uses the most specific matching destination route.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use route tables to determine where traffic leaves a subnet or transit attachment. Security controls…

reveal.text: Use route tables to determine where traffic leaves a subnet or transit attachment. Security controls do not replace a required route.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A private subnet route table contains `10.0.0.0/16 -> local` and `0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-123`.

reveal.text: A private subnet route table contains `10.0.0.0/16 -> local` and `0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-123`. Traffic to another address in the VPC uses the more specific local route; internet-bound IPv4 traffic follows the NAT route.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Correct security rules but no route to the destination -> route table/path issue.

reveal.text: Correct security rules but no route to the destination -> route table/path issue.

prompts.placeholder: Security groups are stateful allow-only controls applied to network interfaces/resources. Network ACLs are stateless subnet…

reveal.text: Security groups are stateful allow-only controls applied to network interfaces/resources. Network ACLs are stateless subnet controls with ordered allow and deny rules.

reveal.text: A security group allows inbound TCP/443 from clients, and response traffic is automatically allowed because the security group is stateful. A NACL is stateless, so its rules must also permit the required return traffic.

nodes.title: Internet gateway, NAT gateway, and egress-only IGW

prompts.label: HOW DO INTERNET GATEWAYS, NAT GATEWAYS, AND EGRESS-ONLY INTERNET GATEWAYS DIFFER?
prompts.placeholder: An internet gateway provides a VPC path to the internet for appropriately addressed/routed resources. A…

reveal.text: An internet gateway gives appropriately addressed and routed VPC resources a path to the internet. A NAT gateway commonly provides outbound internet access for private IPv4 workloads. A NAT gateway can also perform NAT64 so IPv6-only workloads can reach IPv4 destinations when used with DNS64. An egress-only internet gateway provides outbound-only native IPv6 internet connectivity.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Choose by IP version and whether inbound-initiated internet connectivity is required.

reveal.text: Choose by IP version and whether inbound-initiated internet connectivity is required.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A private IPv4 EC2 instance downloads OS patches through a NAT gateway.

reveal.text: A private IPv4 EC2 instance downloads OS patches through a NAT gateway. An IPv6-only workload that must call an IPv4-only service can use DNS64 plus NAT64 through a NAT gateway. A private IPv6 workload that only needs native IPv6 internet egress uses an egress-only internet gateway.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare the main VPC internet-egress choices.

prompts.label: WHAT ARE VPC ENDPOINTS AND AWS PRIVATELINK?
prompts.placeholder: A VPC endpoint lets supported traffic reach AWS or endpoint services privately without using an…

reveal.text: A VPC endpoint provides private connectivity from a VPC to a supported service, endpoint service, or resource without requiring a public internet path. Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB use route tables and do not use AWS PrivateLink. Interface endpoints use private endpoint network interfaces and are powered by AWS PrivateLink.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use gateway endpoints for supported S3/DynamoDB route-table integration; use interface endpoints, powered by PrivateLink, when…

reveal.text: Use gateway endpoints for supported S3/DynamoDB route-table integration; use interface endpoints, powered by PrivateLink, when the supported service is reached through private ENIs in your subnets.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: Private EC2 instances download large amounts from S3.

reveal.text: Private EC2 instances download large amounts from S3. An S3 gateway endpoint lets supported S3 traffic stay on the AWS network without NAT processing. An interface endpoint instead creates private ENIs for supported PrivateLink services.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Gateway endpoint • Interface endpoint

cells.remember: No additional endpoint charge; does not use AWS PrivateLink

prompts.placeholder: A Route 53 hosted zone stores DNS records for a domain. Public hosted zones answer…

reveal.text: A Route 53 hosted zone stores DNS records for a domain. Public hosted zones provide public DNS answers. Private hosted zones provide private answers through VPC Resolver for associated VPCs and can also be queried from connected networks through a properly configured Resolver inbound setup.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use alias records for supported AWS targets when appropriate, including zone-apex cases where a CNAME…

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A private hosted zone contains `db.internal.example.com -> 10.0.20.15` and resolves only inside associated VPCs.

reveal.text: A private hosted zone contains `db.internal.example.com -> 10.0.20.15` for workloads in associated VPCs. An on-premises DNS resolver can also reach those private records through an inbound Resolver endpoint in an associated VPC. A public hosted zone for `www.example.com` answers public-internet DNS queries.

nodes.title: Route 53 routing policies and query logging

prompts.label: WHAT ARE ROUTE 53 ROUTING POLICIES AND QUERY LOGS?
prompts.placeholder: Route 53 routing policies decide how DNS answers are selected. Query logging records DNS-query information…

reveal.text: Route 53 routing policies decide which DNS records Route 53 returns. Public DNS query logging records queries sent to Route 53 authoritative DNS for public hosted zones. Resolver query logging records DNS activity handled by Route 53 Resolver for selected VPC and hybrid paths.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Choose simple, weighted, latency, failover, geolocation, geoproximity, or multivalue behavior based on the routing requirement…

reveal.text: Choose the routing policy from the requirement: simple, weighted, latency, failover, geolocation, geoproximity, IP-based, or multivalue answer routing.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A weighted policy sends 90% of DNS responses to the current version and 10% to a new endpoint.

reveal.text: Weighted records with weights 90 and 10 make Route 53 choose the first record for about 90% of applicable DNS responses and the second for about 10%. This is a DNS-response ratio, not an exact per-request traffic guarantee because clients and recursive resolvers can cache answers. Failover routing instead uses primary/secondary health, while IP-based routing uses client source CIDR mappings that you define.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Relative traffic split -> weighted. Active/passive -> failover. Lowest AWS Region latency -> latency routing. Route known client CIDR ranges using your own mapping -> IP-based routing.

reveal.text: Relative traffic split -> weighted. Active/passive -> failover. Lowest AWS Region latency -> latency routing. Route known client CIDR ranges using your own mapping -> IP-based routing.

A distributed AWS site close to users where services such as CloudFront can receive and serve requests.
The backend source CloudFront contacts when it needs content that is not being served from cache.

reveal.text: A client cannot reach an ALB. DNS resolves correctly, but the subnet route is valid and the security group denies the client port. Walking DNS -> route -> SG/NACL -> target health finds the first failing layer instead of randomly changing settings.

reveal.text: VPC Flow Logs record IP-flow metadata such as addresses, ports, protocol, counters, and ACCEPT/REJECT actions for supported VPC resources. They do not capture application payloads. Some records can be skipped and some derived metadata fields are best-effort, so interpret them together with other troubleshooting evidence.

prompts.label: HOW DO DIRECT CONNECT, SITE-TO-SITE VPN, AND CLIENT VPN DIFFER?
prompts.placeholder: Direct Connect provides dedicated connectivity between customer networks and AWS. Site-to-Site VPN creates IPsec network-to-network…

reveal.text: Direct Connect provides dedicated connectivity between customer networks and AWS. Site-to-Site VPN creates IPsec network-to-network connectivity over the internet. Client VPN provides secure remote-user/device access.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?

reveal.text: Choose based on who is connecting and whether dedicated private connectivity or internet-based encrypted connectivity is required.

reveal.text: A data center needs stable dedicated connectivity for large daily transfers: Direct Connect may fit. A branch office needs encrypted network-to-network connectivity over the internet: Site-to-Site VPN. Remote employees need user VPN access: Client VPN.

prompts.label: WHAT ARE THE CLOUDWATCH NETWORK MONITORING SERVICES?
prompts.placeholder: CloudWatch network monitoring services observe different parts of network health: Network Flow Monitor focuses on…

reveal.text: CloudWatch Network Monitoring includes Network Flow Monitor, Internet Monitor, and Network Synthetic Monitor. Network Flow Monitor uses agents on supported EC2 and EKS compute to collect TCP flow performance statistics. Internet Monitor measures how internet performance and availability affect application users. Network Synthetic Monitor uses AWS-managed probes from selected VPC subnets to on-premises destinations, with no workload agent installation required.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Choose based on whether the problem is workload flow performance, internet user experience, or a…

reveal.text: Choose the service from the question: actual workload TCP-flow performance, end-user internet impact, or proactive hybrid-path latency and packet-loss testing.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: Users in one geography report high latency to the public application while the AWS resources are healthy.

reveal.text: Users in one geography report slow access to a public application while its AWS resources are healthy. Internet Monitor can show internet-path impact. For a hybrid path, Network Synthetic Monitor can probe from a selected VPC subnet to an on-premises IP and report latency and packet loss. CloudWatch Synthetics canaries are different: they run scheduled scripts that test endpoints and APIs.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare Network Flow Monitor, Internet Monitor, Network Synthetic Monitor, and CloudWatch Synthetics.
